title: Seven lines of unknown signs in the margin of a printed Latin book (user-supplied photograph, provenance unknown)

documents.shelfmark: unknown (photograph supplied by the user, 16 Oct 2026; targets/bookmargin/margin.png)

plaintext.source: No decipherment, key or clear copy known.

transcription.notes: Provisional sign classes; interlinear signs omitted; the arch-shaped family may be split or merged wrongly. Not checked by a second reader.

system.summary: Left-to-right signs resembling Ethiopic fidel (or Samaritan letters), with barred numeral-like signs and four-dot marks; system and language not established.
system.notes: If the signs are Ethiopic the text may be a Ge'ez note rather than a cipher.

prior_solution.where: No reading found by web search (16 Oct 2026).

conditions.human_role: Supplied the photograph with the request to solve it; no provenance or other help.

solution.what: Searched the repository, catalogue.json and the web (Schmeh's Encrypted Book List, Cipher Mysteries) for the image or a description of it.

Compared the signs with rendered charts of Samaritan, Phoenician, Ethiopic, Glagolitic, Tibetan, Old Italic, Old Hungarian, Georgian and Armenian; Ethiopic fits best (arch letters, ተ, ገ, ለ, አ, ። and numeral bars), Samaritan second; the commonest sign has no clear counterpart.
Tested the image rotated 180 degrees as upside-down Latin script.
Segmented the glyphs automatically and transcribed 174 signs into provisional classes from contact sheets.
Simple substitution into Latin (CLTK Caesar/Cicero/Sallust quadgrams), 12 annealing restarts, one-to-one key on the commonest classes.
Same solver on three shuffles of the transcription: shuffled -12.46 to -12.62 per quadgram against real -12.86, so the Latin fit is no better than chance.

outcome.method_basis: Script provisionally identified; no key, reading or language established; Latin substitution scored no better than shuffled controls.
outcome.notes: In progress: provenance of the image unknown; Ethiopic hypothesis to be tested on a Ge'ez corpus.

gaps.detail: needs a Ge'ez reader or a sharper image
